screening_decisions.reason: Prospective pelvic mass cohort; preoperative HE4/CA125 measured and combined as ROMA, compared with RMI; histopathologic outcomes reported; evaluates biomarker–ultrasound combinations relevant to review.

Prospective cross-sectional study of women undergoing surgery for pelvic mass; HE4, CA125, and ROMA evaluated against final pathology. Includes healthy controls but primary analysis is adnexal masses.
Diagnostic accuracy study in surgically managed adnexal masses with histology reference; validates IOTA ADNEX model with/without CA125; aligns with ultrasound–biomarker model focus.
Retrospective audit of CA125 test utilization across general patients (includes males); not a DTA study in women with pelvic masses and lacks appropriate reference standard.
Retrospective diagnostic accuracy using prospectively collected data; compares ADNEX, LR2, simple rules, and RMI in patients with adnexal masses; pathology is reference standard.
Systematic review/meta-analysis; not a primary DTA study of individual patients.
Surgically managed adnexal mass cohort; RMI 1–4 computed using ultrasound, menopausal status, and CA125; histopathology reference; provides accuracy stratified by menopausal status.
Prospective multicenter evaluation of HE4, CA125, and ROMA with analyses by menopausal status and benign pelvic mass vs EOC; likely histological confirmation; relevant biomarker combinations.
Mixed population including healthy women and diverse gynecologic diseases (e.g., myomas) not restricted to adnexal masses suspicious for OC; unclear DTA design in the target clinical population.
Narrative/systematic review of symptoms, not a primary DTA study of the specified index tests with a histologic reference.
Systematic review/meta-analysis; not primary patient-level DTA.
Epidemiological burden paper; not a DTA study or validation of index test combinations.
Large prospective multicentre DTA of the IOTA ADNEX model incorporating CA125 and ultrasound predictors; histology reference; directly aligned with target index test combinations.
Retrospective series of surgically treated adnexal neoplasms with histology; compares CA125, HE4, ROMA, RMI-II with analyses by menopausal status; meets DTA criteria.
Prospective case-control including women with adnexal masses (benign and malignant) with histology plus healthy controls; evaluates HE4+CA125 and ROMA; relevant to index test combinations.
Preoperative serum biomarkers in cohorts including benign cysts/endometriosis and EOC; evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA with menopausal stratification; diagnostic component aligns with review scope.
Prospective multicentre DTA comparing IOTA ultrasound-based strategies and RMI in surgically managed adnexal masses with histology; directly relevant.
Original RMI development paper combining CA125, ultrasound, and menopausal status in women with pelvic masses; histology reference; cornerstone DTA study for review topic.
Biomarker expression/biology (immunohistochemistry) study; no clinical DTA in women with adnexal masses.
Hospital cohort classified into malignant, benign, and borderline groups by pathology; compares CA125, HE4, ROMA with analyses by menopausal status; fits DTA scope.
Prospective cohort of women with suspicious ovarian cysts undergoing surgery; HE4/CA125 (and ROMA) evaluated against histology; appropriate population and index tests.

Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA in ovarian cancer vs benign gynecologic disease with reported cut-offs and performance; although includes healthy controls, it assesses diagnostic discrimination relevant to adnexal pathology.
Prospective validation in women with adnexal masses undergoing surgery; ultrasound-based simple rules compared with other models; histology reference; matches ultrasound index tests.
Cross-sectional DTA of ROMA (HE4+CA125+menopausal status) in postmenopausal women with ovarian masses, with histopathology as reference.
Cancer incidence/mortality projection modeling; not a diagnostic accuracy study in pelvic mass patients and no index test evaluation.
Qualitative study of patient experiences; no evaluation of diagnostic tests or accuracy against a reference standard.
Narrative/annual review on ovarian cancer biology and heterogeneity; not a primary DTA study of tests in women with a pelvic mass.
Nested case–control using prediagnostic samples (screening/lead-time) from a general cohort; not symptomatic pelvic mass patients undergoing diagnostic work-up.
Methodology paper (QUADAS-2) for bias assessment; not a primary DTA study in the target population.
Validation of ROMA cut-points using Roche Elecsys CA125 and HE4 assays in 207 women with pelvic mass, with definitive histology as reference.
Review of CA125 literature; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study in the target population.
Review proposing a tumorigenesis model; no patient-level diagnostic accuracy evaluation.
Critical review of proteomics; not a primary DTA study of specified index tests in pelvic mass patients.
Cross-sectional validation of the Risk of Malignancy Index (combining CA125, ultrasound, menopausal status) against histopathology in women with adnexal masses.
ROMA evaluated in 443 women with a pelvic mass, compared with biopsy or clinical follow-up; meets DTA criteria with acceptable reference standards.
Preoperative assessment comparing expert ultrasound, CA-125, RMI, and combinations in 1362 surgically explored adnexal masses; stratified by menopausal status; histology reference.
Prospective multicenter cross-sectional DTA of IOTA ultrasound descriptors/rules with histological diagnosis of surgically removed masses; compares to RMI.
Methodological assessment of publication bias tests in DTA meta-analyses; not a primary clinical DTA study.
Evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA in patients with pelvic masses with AUC analyses and proposed cut-offs; consistent with DTA of biomarkers in the target population.
External validation of the IOTA ADNEX (ultrasound-based multivariable) model in patients with adnexal masses; diagnostic performance vs histology.
Service evaluation of symptom-triggered testing implementation and outcomes; does not report diagnostic accuracy of index tests vs a reference standard in pelvic mass patients.
Multicenter prospective validation of a HE4+CA125 algorithm (separate models by menopausal status) in women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; DTA metrics reported.
Guideline on evaluation/management; not a primary diagnostic accuracy study.
Molecular genetics (ARID1A) study; not evaluating diagnostic test accuracy in pelvic mass patients.
Appears to be a narrative overview/commentary on HE4 vs traditional markers; no clear primary DTA in the target population.
Prospective multicenter study in Asian women with pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA performance against surgical diagnosis.
Population registry incidence trends; no diagnostic test accuracy evaluation, no index tests or histology/clinical follow-up in women with a pelvic mass.
Secondary research (systematic review/meta-analysis); protocol includes primary cross-sectional DTA studies, RCTs, or model validation only.
Prospective cross-sectional DTA in women with adnexal masses scheduled for surgery; index tests CA125, HE4, and ROMA; reference standard histopathology; analyses stratified by menopausal status.

Prospective multicentre cross-sectional validation in women with adnexal masses; tests: IOTA LR2, Simple Rules, RMI, and subjective assessment; surgical histology as reference; performance also reported by menopausal status.
Meta-analysis (secondary research); not a primary DTA study in women with a pelvic mass.

Prospective, cross-sectional DTA in women undergoing surgery for ovarian lesions; preoperative pelvic ultrasound and biomarkers (CA-125, HE4) with composite indices (RMI, ROMA); histopathology as reference; includes menopausal subgroups.
Multicentre study of patients with suspicious pelvic masses requiring surgery; evaluates HE4, CA125, ROMA with stratification by menopausal status; histologically verified outcomes.
Methodological paper on meta-analytic modeling; no patient cohort, no index tests applied to pelvic masses.
Simulation/methods-focused meta-analytic modeling paper; not a primary DTA study in women with a pelvic mass.
Genetic predisposition study; not an accuracy study of diagnostic tests in women presenting with a pelvic mass.
Narrative review; no primary cross-sectional DTA or test comparison in pelvic mass populations.
Prospective, multicentre, blinded DTA validation of ROMA in women with a pelvic mass; preoperative HE4+CA125; histopathology reference; menopausal subgroup performance reported.
Prospective study of women undergoing surgical exploration of pelvic masses; compares RMI 1–4 (combining menopausal status, CA125, USS) against histology; reports sensitivity/specificity.
Postmenopausal women with adnexal masses who underwent surgery; evaluates RMI (1–4) and CA-125 (and inflammatory markers) versus histopathology; DTA design within target population.

Preoperative serum HE4, CA125, and ROMA to distinguish benign ovarian disease from epithelial ovarian cancer; DTA metrics and menopausal stratification reported; consistent with surgical histology as reference.
Primary care symptom case-control; not limited to women with a pelvic mass and no index test vs histology/clinical follow-up comparison.
Prospective validation in women with a pelvic mass scheduled for surgery; preoperative HE4+CA125 and ROMA; histopathology reference; menopausal cutoffs used.
Systematic review/meta-analysis; not a primary cross-sectional DTA or RCT/model validation study on index patients.
Patients with ovarian masses assessed for CA125, HE4, ROMA, and RMI; DTA performance reported; reference standard likely histopathology in this surgical cohort. Included conservatively.
Guideline/commentary on hereditary risk; not a diagnostic accuracy study on pelvic mass evaluation.
Cross-sectional study in 277 patients with ovarian masses; preoperative CA-125, HE4, ROMA compared with postoperative histopathology; reports AUC and performance overall and by menopausal status.
Postmenopausal cohort with ovarian cancer vs benign ovarian tumors; all diagnoses histologically verified; pre-treatment serum HE4, CA125, ROMA2; DTA in target population.
Preoperative evaluation in mainly postmenopausal women with supposed ovarian tumors; compares 2D/3D Doppler US, RMI, IOTA Simple Rules/LR2, CA125 against histology; DTA design.
Systematic review/meta-analysis comparing HE4 vs CA-125; not a primary cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study in symptomatic pelvic mass.

Diagnostic accuracy study enrolling 129 women with suspected ovarian pelvic masses scheduled for surgery/biopsy; evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA with sensitivity/specificity and ROC—meets population, index tests, and reference standard.
Prospective study of women with complex pelvic masses; preoperative HE4, CA125, ROMA, and RMI with performance metrics; histology implied—fits cross-sectional DTA in symptomatic masses.
Methodological tool (PROBAST) for risk of bias/applicability; not a primary ovarian mass diagnostic accuracy study.

Women with pelvic masses scheduled for surgery plus healthy controls; evaluates HE4, CA125, and ROMA with AUC and sensitivity/specificity (pre/postmenopausal). Despite healthy controls, core analysis involves surgical pelvic masses with likely histologic reference—include.
Epidemiologic/methods study on routes to cancer diagnosis using routine datasets; not a DTA study of ovarian mass tests.
Statistical methodology (bivariate meta-regression vs sROC) paper; not a primary DTA study in ovarian masses.

Prospective population-based recruitment of women with pelvic mass scheduled for surgery across multiple hospitals; compares RMI vs ROMA and CA125 vs HE4 with defined cut-offs—meets cross-sectional DTA in symptomatic masses with histology.
Software user guide (MetaDAS) for meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy; not a primary clinical DTA study.
Meta-analysis of ROMA, HE4, and CA125; secondary synthesis, not a primary cross-sectional DTA in symptomatic pelvic masses.

Multicenter IOTA database analysis of 2445 adnexal masses with histological reference; evaluates ultrasound-based models (LR1/LR2), IOTA simple rules, and RMI with performance metrics—fits cross-sectional DTA in surgical adnexal masses.
Subset analysis of a prospective trial in premenopausal women undergoing surgery for adnexal mass; compares HE4 vs CA-125 specificity/sensitivity—meets DTA criteria in symptomatic masses.
Focus on EOC prediction plus therapy-monitoring/prognosis; case/control-type sample (EOC patients vs controls), not clearly women with symptomatic pelvic mass undergoing diagnostic workup.
Benign gynecologic disorders only; no malignant comparator in this analysis; not a diagnostic accuracy study for detecting ovarian cancer.
Narrative review of biomarkers for screening/diagnosis/monitoring; not primary DTA research in symptomatic pelvic masses.
Assay development/validation (ELISA) with case-control comparisons; not a clinical cross-sectional DTA in women presenting with pelvic mass.
Systematic review of risk scores; not primary diagnostic accuracy in a new sample of symptomatic pelvic mass patients.
Target condition is endometrial cancer; assesses sentinel node biopsy—wrong disease focus for ovarian cancer mass diagnosis.
Paper includes a prospective validation study (303 women) of IOTA simple rules with histology, alongside a meta-analysis. The embedded primary validation fits cross-sectional DTA in adnexal tumors.

Korean study includes 762 benign gynecologic disease patients and 70 ovarian cancers; not clearly restricted to symptomatic pelvic masses under diagnostic workup nor clear histology for all benign comparators—population likely outside protocol.
Review comparing indices (IOTA LR2, ROMA, RMI, etc.); not a primary cross-sectional DTA study.
Multicenter clinical validation in women with unknown ovarian cyst/pelvic tumor preoperatively; compares HE4, CA125, ROMA, RMI vs final pathology—fits cross-sectional DTA with surgical reference.

ADNEX model vs subjective assessment in 353 women undergoing adnexal surgery after abnormal ultrasound; AUC, sensitivity/specificity reported—validates a multivariable model in symptomatic adnexal masses.
